problem:
The position $s(t)$ of a particle (in meters) at time $t$ seconds is given by 

$$
s(t)=6\operatorname{ln}⁡t-3{t}^{2},\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the speed of the particle when $t=2\,\text{s}.$

The speed of the particle is 
{{field-1}}$\text{m/s}.$
worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6\operatorname{ln}⁡t-3{t}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{6}{t}-6t\end{aligned}
$$

When $t=2,$ the velocity is

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =\frac{6}{2}-6(2) \\  & =-9.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the speed is $|-9|=9\,\text{m/s}.$
